# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

**From:** Taylor Foster
Member ID: W492196775
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-24 — Reference number POC-C65CA65DA3-33163**
**Service denied:** Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
**Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), state of Wyoming
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0736 – Hip Preservation Surgery (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0736.html)

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of the hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) that my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Okafor, requested for me. Aetna denied the request on 2026-08-24, stating that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure, because my records show a long and well-documented course of non-surgical treatment that did not resolve my symptoms.

## A note about the policy language

I want to be straightforward with the reviewer about one thing. The portions of Aetna CPB 0736 – Hip Preservation Surgery that I have in front of me do not include the specific conservative-care requirement for hip arthroscopy that the denial relies on. I am therefore not going to put words in the plan's mouth. Where I quote below, the words are copied exactly from the policy. Where the policy has not been quoted to me, I say so plainly and make the point in my own words, and I ask that the reviewer compare my records directly against the arthroscopy criteria in the policy itself.

## The criteria I can quote, and what my records show

**1. Duration of symptoms.** The policy states:

> "and Minimum 6 months of symptoms;"

My records establish far more than this. The prior authorization packet documents **24 months of progressive pain in the hip, unrelieved by rest.** That is four times the minimum duration the plan sets out in its own published criteria.

**2. Condition of the joint.** The policy states:

> "for members with moderate or worse arthritis (Tonnis 2 or 3), the procedure would be considered not medically necessary;"

My records establish the opposite of that exclusion. My MRI arthrogram of 2026-07-11 shows **joint space preserved, Tonnis grade 0**. The same study documents an **anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, alpha angle 68 degrees**. There is no arthritis finding in my chart that would place me in the group the policy excludes.

**3. What the plan itself treats as an adequate conservative trial.** For a different procedure within this same policy, Aetna defines the conservative-care threshold in specific terms:

> "Endoscopic tenotomy (or lengthening) for iliopsoas tendinopathy following total hip arthroplasty with the failure of at least 6 weeks of formal in-person physical therapy in the past year, and at least 1 therapeutic injection (steroid with or without local anesthetic) with significant but temporary benefit in the past 6 months."

I understand that this sentence describes a different operation and is not the rule being applied to me. I raise it only because it shows the scale of conservative treatment this policy regards as sufficient — six weeks of in-person physical therapy and one therapeutic injection. My documented course exceeds that benchmark:

- **Supervised physical therapy:** core and hip stabilization with activity modification, **14 weeks (2026-04-27 to 2026-08-03), 18 visits completed**, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** **NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.**
- **Injection:** **corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-14, giving 4 weeks of partial relief** — significant but temporary, and then the pain returned.

**4. How the policy says these criteria were built.** The policy states:

> "These supplemental medical necessity criteria are based upon evidence-based guidelines and clinical studies in the peer-reviewed published medical literature."

I am asking only that those criteria be applied to what is actually in my chart.

## Why I believe the conservative-care finding should be revisited

The denial says my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. My records document 14 weeks and 18 visits of supervised physical therapy, eight months of anti-inflammatory medication, activity modification, and a steroid injection that helped for four weeks and then wore off. I did all of it, in order, before anyone discussed surgery with me.

My records also show where that left me: **sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and an inability to run or squat.** On examination I have **positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.** I have **no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.**

My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is needed. If the reviewer still concludes that my conservative care was inadequate, I respectfully ask to be told, in writing, which specific element of the arthroscopy criteria in CPB 0736 my documentation falls short of, and what the required duration or modality is — so that I can respond to a stated standard rather than a general conclusion.

## What I am requesting

I ask that Aetna:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-24 (reference POC-C65CA65DA3-33163) and authorize hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with orthopedic surgery experience;
3. Review the enclosed records in full; and
4. If the denial is upheld, identify the exact criterion in Aetna CPB 0736 – Hip Preservation Surgery that my records do not satisfy, and provide me with a copy of that criterion and with information about my further appeal rights.

**Enclosures:** copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-24; physical therapy discharge note (18 visits, 2026-04-27 to 2026-08-03); MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-07-11; injection record dated 2026-06-14; office notes from Dr. Okafor; [any other records I am including].

## Filing details

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-20** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I am submitting it using Aetna's **Member Complaint and Appeal Form**, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, and sending it by **fax to 859-425-3379** or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I have confirmed. Aetna member services can also be reached at **1-800-872-3862** or the number on my card.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. Please contact me at the phone number above if anything further is needed.

Sincerely,

 

_____________________________
**Taylor Foster**
Member ID: W492196775
Date of birth: [My date of birth]
Date: [Date signed]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
